headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad egress and browser use can feed social-auto-upload workflows, creating default data-leak and compliance risks; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and ingest web content, while social-auto-upload operates on account workflows and files. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; however, if RD-Agent’s browser output is copied into B’s upload/account workflow, malicious content could influence actions. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF RD-Agent browser output is manually copied into social-auto-upload inputs
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted content source
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not copy browser-sourced text into upload prompts
Review any generated captions or metadata before upload
Use a human approval step for all B-side actions

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, logs, and research data and has broad network egress; social-auto-upload touches account data and also has broad egress. A shared workspace is not documented, but if either agent is given the same files or credentials, sensitive material can flow out through networked APIs. This is a plausible default-path risk, not a proven one.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same directory or account files
IF either agent is configured with sensitive reports or account data
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials
Remove sensitive files from shared locations
Disable network access for test runs where possible
Rotate any exposed API keys or account tokens
Audit outbound requests before enabling production runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, while social-auto-upload explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. A conflict could still arise if both are orchestrated over the same mutable account files or external API state, but the profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable account file or external resource
IF RD-Agent writes logs into a directory B also reads or syncs
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize access to any shared account file
Avoid concurrent runs against the same external account
Keep RD-Agent logs out of B’s input paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs and logs, and social-auto-upload can act on account workflows. If B consumes A’s generated content without verification, a bad fact or malformed artifact can cascade into an incorrect upload or account-side action. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses RD-Agent outputs as upload-ready content
IF no human or automated verification step checks A’s outputs before B acts
mitigations: Add a validation step before upload
Require human review of A-generated artifacts
Reject outputs that fail schema or checksum checks
Log provenance for every file passed from A to B

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports and logs and requests multiple third-party API keys; social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to external platforms. The pair can therefore mix regulated or sensitive data with third-party processing. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF financial reports or personal account data are processed through third-party APIs
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the shared data flow
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Exclude regulated data from social upload workflows
Document retention and deletion handling
Use separate API credentials per environment
Review vendor terms for each external API
